physics_goals.quote: we measure the lowest rates in silicon detectors of events containing one, two, three, or four electrons, and achieve world-leading sensitivity for a large range of sub-GeV dark matter masses
value: Detect sub-GeV dark matter via electron-recoil ionization signals in skipper-CCD silicon detectors

summary.plain: SENSEI uses ultra-sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs to hunt for very light dark matter particles, so light that they would only knock loose a handful of electrons. It has run in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab near Chicago since 2018.
summary.technical: Skipper-CCD dark matter search sensitive to electron recoils from sub-GeV dark matter, operating in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab; began with a ~0.1 g prototype device (2018-2019 shallow-underground run) and progressed to an improved ~2 g Skipper-CCD (2020 results), with operations continuing as of a 2026 backgrounds-characterization paper. A ~100 g detector at SNOLAB was described as planned in 2020 but not confirmed as realized by any source fetched this session.

unique_capabilities.quote: We find zero events with three (or more) electrons in the unblinded data
value: Skipper-CCD readout allows sub-electron noise, enabling counting of individual ionization electrons (SENSEI's 2019 shallow-underground run found zero three-or-more-electron events in its unblinded data)
